title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Garden Auditorium on 1966-07-30

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a primitive yet thrilling 1966 Vancouver show, highlighted by an incendiary Cream Puff War and a wild Viola Lee Blues.
ai_review.review: The upgraded FLAC offers an exceptionally clear mix for a 1966 soundboard tape, letting the early Dead’s raw energy shine through. Reviewers rave about the soaring Cream Puff War and the freak‑out version of Viola Lee Blues, while noting the show’s solid pacing despite its nascent stage. A few dissenting voices criticize the overall performance, but the consensus is that this recording is a must‑have for collectors.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers award 4–5 stars and praise both the performance and the surprisingly pristine soundboard source; only a minority give low scores, resulting in an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clear, crisp mix despite being over four decades old; upgraded mastering praised as ‘SMOKIN’ and ‘polished gem’, with no reported dropouts or balance issues.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid early‑Dead set from Vancouver that pushes further than the previous night, maintaining high energy and primitive improvisation while delivering memorable climaxes.

band_member_comments.Phil: Multiple reviewers note a ‘Phil bomb’ and love his intro on Cream Puff War.
